title: Yemen separatists urge US not to let Saudi Arabia ‘call the shots’
gist: STC foreign affairs representative Amr al-Bidh argues that the Saudi counteroffensive that crushed the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council left a security vacuum the Houthis exploited to seize Yemen's Red Sea coast and Bab el-Mandeb islands, and urges Washington to broker a comprehensive settlement including southern self-determination rather than 'letting the Saudis call the shots.'

insights.claim: STC representative Amr al-Bidh argues the Saudi counteroffensive against the STC, not the STC's expansion, created the vacuum that allowed the Houthis to escalate around the Red Sea.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: If correct, Saudi-led consolidation of the anti-Houthi camp has weakened deterrence, making Red Sea disruption stickier.
insights.quote: Without having the deterrence on the ground, it was a recipe for the Houthis to move ahead.

insights.claim: The Saudi-led military restructuring left southern Yemen without a unified security force, creating openings for both the Houthis and al-Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Fragmented southern forces raise terrorism and piracy risk around the Gulf of Aden.

insights.claim: After the STC's December offensive captured oil-rich Hadhramaut and al-Mahrah, a Saudi-backed government counteroffensive reversed the gains within weeks, the UAE withdrew its remaining forces, and the STC announced its dissolution, which Bidh says was coerced by Riyadh.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: The Saudi-UAE split over Yemen is a key Gulf fault line with implications for Yemeni oil assets and Gulf cohesion.

insights.claim: The Houthis seized the port city of Mokha, the volcanic island of Mayyun in the Bab el Mandeb Strait, and the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands in the southern Red Sea, while advancing toward Taiz.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Houthi control of islands in the strait gives them persistent ability to threaten shipping; keep Red Sea rerouting assumptions.

insights.claim: Roughly 10% of global maritime trade passes through the 32-kilometer-wide Bab el Mandeb connecting the Red Sea and the Gulf of Aden.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: A sustained Bab el Mandeb disruption affects a tenth of global maritime trade, lifting freight rates and insurance costs.

insights.claim: Analysts expect the Houthis to focus near-term on consolidating their newly captured coastal corridor; if they push further south, Bidh expects fragmented southern factions to unite against them.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: A consolidation pause may temporarily cap escalation, but a southward push would trigger wider fighting near Aden.

insights.claim: Trump has reportedly rebuffed Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's appeals for US military intervention, reluctant to resume a bombing campaign that ended in May 2025 with an Oman-mediated US-Houthi truce.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: No US military backstop for Saudi Arabia in Yemen; Gulf security risk rests on regional actors.

insights.claim: US Embassy personnel met Houthi officials, including spokesperson Mohammad Abdulsalam, in Muscat; the Houthis reportedly said they did not plan to attack US vessels and remain committed to the US-Houthi ceasefire.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: US-flagged shipping may face lower Houthi risk than Saudi-linked shipping, a differentiated risk for carriers.

insights.claim: Bidh says there is no sole military solution to the Houthis and urges the Trump administration to adopt a comprehensive approach involving local and regional actors rather than just letting the Saudis call the shots.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Signals UAE-aligned actors lobbying Washington to dilute Saudi control over Yemen policy.
insights.quote: There is no sole military solution. It’s been tried and not worked.

insights.claim: The STC argues an independent South Yemen, as existed from 1967 to 1990, would serve as a buffer zone against Houthi expansion, and seeks a negotiated settlement recognizing the south's right to decide its future.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Yemen partition scenarios remain live, affecting control of Aden port and southern oil provinces.

insights.claim: STC leader Aidarous al-Zubaidi had proposed a two-year transition toward an independence referendum and is now in an undisclosed location, per Bidh.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: Leadership disarray limits the STC's near-term capacity to act as a counterweight.

insights.claim: Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry announced in January a planned dialogue conference with Yemen's southern factions, but no date has been set.
insights.speaker: Elizabeth Hagedorn
insights.so_what: A scheduled southern dialogue would be a de-escalation signal to watch for.
